data.narrative:
Code Metal, a Series B defense and security company founded by Peter Morales and Alex Showalter-Bucher, is evaluated against a peer universe of 10 comparable companies: 2 public (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS) and 8 private firms. The target's last post-money valuation stands at $1.2B on $161M total raised.

Two valuation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis uses a 1.9x multiplier typical for Series B-to-next-stage advancement, yielding $2.4B. Peer-median benchmarking across 6 same-sector, same-stage comparables—including Dream Security ($3.0B), Harmattan AI ($1.4B), Castelion ($1.0B), Defense Unicorns ($1.0B), and Heven AeroTech ($1.0B)—produces a median valuation of $1.0B, with a range of $300M to $3.0B. The discrepancy between methods reflects dispersion in the peer set and the volatility typical of early-stage frontier defense tech.

Triangulation of these two approaches supports a valuation range of $850M to $2.7B, with a median implied value of $1.7B. The current $1.25B post-money valuation sits within this range, slightly below the median. Key uncertainties include the sustainability of growth rates relative to peer cohorts and the timing of revenue inflection relative to capital deployment. The 19-point spread between peer minimum and maximum suggests substantial heterogeneity in investor expectations within this sector.
